verdict: OpenCart: Choose OpenCart when you want a free PHP open-source cart and will own hosting and extensions — not when you need WordPress-native WooCommerce or hosted SaaS simplicity. Scores use the Ecommerce editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Commerce-first PHP cart (not a CMS plugin)
Low license floor for self-hosted SMBs
weaknesses: Managed cloud pricing needs live confirmation
bestFor: SMB merchants wanting a free PHP open-source cart
Teams comfortable self-hosting and buying extensions
Catalogs that do not need Magento/Adobe programme depth
notIdealFor: Founders wanting zero hosting ops (see Shopify)
Retailers whose center of gravity is POS hardware
tradeoffs: Subscription floors vs payment-processing spreads and GMV/overage fees
App/extension TCO vs native feature depth
Open-source/hosting flexibility vs SaaS operational simplicity
Dropshipping product caps vs catalog automation depth
recommendation: Choose OpenCart when you want a free PHP open-source cart and will own hosting and extensions — not when you need WordPress-native WooCommerce or hosted SaaS simplicity. Consider WooCommerce for WordPress-native open source; PrestaShop for EU commerce-first PHP; Magento for deeper B2B/enterprise; Shopify for hosted SaaS.
editorialNotes: Ecommerce Priority-3 batch. Approved on ecommerce-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=open-source-platform. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: More approachable than Magento for simple PHP stores; still self-hosted ops versus Shopify/Woo guided paths.
Core job is open-source storefront. Landscape peer — WooCommerce keeps the open-source cluster award (8.1).
Solid catalog and order basics for SMB PHP carts; weaker than Magento for complex B2B programmes.
Checkout works via payment extensions; conversion quality depends on theme and gateway work.
Extension marketplace covers common payments and shipping — narrower mindshare than WooCommerce.
Not a retail POS product — in-person selling is extension territory at best.
Fine for SMB catalogs; high-GMV complex programmes usually outgrow classic OpenCart stacks.
Free GPL core is strong when you accept hosting/extension TCO and do not need Magento depth.
Minimal first-party AI versus modern SaaS platforms.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine ecommerce editorial criteria using category weights (storefront/commerce fit 15, catalog/orders 14, ease 12, checkout 12, integrations 12, value 12, omnichannel/POS 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — SaaS platforms, open-source carts, omnichannel POS bundles, and dropshipping sourcing apps are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score; affiliate economics are excluded.
